Where does it say OSC133 should behave this way? We can't introduce our own semantics into sequences we don't create. If this isn't specified or done by other terminals, I think you should make a broader proposal to terminals to get buy-in first. This kind of stuck can have ripple effects.

Fwiw this sounds like a bug in SSH to me. SSH should probably reset all terminal state to the prior state before connection is made (`ssh` itself runs host side, of course). Or even shells. 

This doesn't like a robust solution either, because nested OSC133 may actually want mouse reporting on (imagine e.g. a nested REPL using `aid` within Neovim or something). You wouldn't want a stray OSC133 in a nested prompt to clear all mouse reporting.

So, if this is done by other terminals and the spec, I'll accept the shortcomings, but if its not, then I think this is a weak proposal.
